notes: RETRACTION of PS-S2-20260924-H8-transition-cache-0014 (NOT_YET_JUSTIFIED, with 0.0136 vs without 0.0136, delta 0.0). No eviction policy ran: keep was computed as a quarter of the held-out LOOKUP count (4474) while the cache held 416 entries, so _require_keep returned surplus 0 and forget_low_utility_memory, lru_control and random_control all took their early exit and evicted nothing. The two arms were bit-identical floats (S2-FC-04). RE-MEASURED this session with keep taken from the cache's own occupancy (416 entries, keep=104): 312 evictions on each of the three policies; utility 0.0134652, lru 0.0134652, random 0.0. The utility-vs-LRU verdict is unchanged at NOT_YET_JUSTIFIED, but it is now a measurement rather than an identity. Also corrected under S2-03: lru_control sorted on last_sequence, which is written only at store time, so the declared LRU control was insertion-order for any re-read workload.

notes: RETRACTION of PS-S2-20260924-H8-causal-credit-0016 (REJECTED, with 0.0 vs without 1.0, delta -1.0). That row measured a dictionary join that can never match, not the mechanism: nodes were keyed by CausalNode.signature (16 hex) and looked up by probe.target_signature, a positional locator 'lineage:index:rN:mM' whose own docstring calls it 'provenance for the probe itself, never an identity the ledger trusts'. assign_causal_credit was therefore never called once, and both gate_criteria.py and stage2_report.py carried the identical defective line, so their agreement was never a cross-check (S2-FC-01). RE-MEASURED this session with the join on the probed transition's real causal signature, same corpus (drift, count=24, seed=11), same probe budget: 6 sessions, ledger chain recall 0.3518 vs naive ancestry 1.0, delta -0.6482, 0/6 sessions more concise at equal or better recall. The verdict stays REJECTED and the mechanism is now genuinely measured; the -1.0 delta and the gate's stated cause ('no probe's divergence reached MATERIAL_DIVERGENCE') were both false.
title: RETRACTS PS-S2-20260924-H8-causal-credit-0016

notes: RETRACTION of PS-S2-20260924-H8-multiscale-window-0013 (NOT_YET_JUSTIFIED, with 0.4928 vs without 0.4926, delta 0.0002). That row did not measure WindowStore, the component it named. _family_sequences grouped relation families by SESSION while WindowStore keys on the causal-signature root, so the (1,2,4) offsets were fed a stream the store never produces; replacing WindowStore with a stub that held nothing returned bit-identical accuracies, and the measuring function's own docstring admitted 'the accuracy figures would be the same for any component that supplied the same taps' while core_ids named DTL-F03 (S2-FC-12). RE-MEASURED this session with per-lineage grouping (3576 lineages, mean length 5.0, against 240 sessions of mean length 73.3), same offsets, same split: 0.5912 with the taps vs 0.7099 at window=1, delta -0.1187. The verdict moves from NOT_YET_JUSTIFIED to REJECTED: the store's extra taps are a measured LOSS for next-family top-1, not a null. SEPARATELY MEASURED, because ADR-0123 decision 3 acts on this row: truncating every lineage window to its last step drops the exported Phi-oracle candidate (DeterministicScorerSpec, max_over_window) from average precision 0.5975 to 0.3243 on ambiguous count=240 seed=11, changing 168/240 session scores. Narrow the taps, do not delete the window.
title: RETRACTS PS-S2-20260924-H8-multiscale-window-0013

notes: CellPathBaseline returns 1.0 for all 60 evaluation sessions, benign and malicious alike, so its PR-AUC equals the base rate BY CONSTRUCTION and measures no discriminative capacity; PhiOracleUnchanged separates the classes completely (benign 0.2000-0.2195, malicious 0.3333-0.5224). Cause: the PCB ISA defines no division opcode, so |dPhi|/(|dPhi|+8) is inexpressible and the verified program is clamp01(dPhi), which saturates at 1.0 on every session here. SEPARATELY: a CellBoundary over all nine DIMENSIONS claims 8 index keys and is ACCEPTED by BoundaryIndex, at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 9 dimensions alike. labs/cell_path.py's docstrings claim 2 dims = 32 keys, 3 dims = 64 keys and 9 dims = 4096 keys refused at MAX_KEYS_PER_CELL=64, and derive from that the structural result that a global rule cannot be crystallised as one cell. That derivation is contradicted by this measurement; the same defect class was already retracted for threat case T7 and the repair was not propagated here.
title: The Phi-oracle Knowledge Cell emits a constant score, and the 4096-key claim is false

notes: docs/stage-3-findings.md published run/_execute = 4.06x and run/handwritten = 235.05x, and cited pocketsec/stage3/bytecode/verifier.py for a '2.9-4.9x band' that file does not report - it records two points across a code change (10.18x while run() decoded twice, 2.93x after) and the string '4.9' appears nowhere in the repository. Neither ratio had a producer, which is the defect the same document's Corrections table forbids. The producer is now pocketsec/stage3/bytecode/cost.py:measure_vm_cost, run by 'python -m pocketsec.stage3.cli vmcost'. Five repeats of the identical procedure in one process, 512 drift-corpus frames, best-of-7 each, loadavg 23.96 before and 23.26 after: run/_execute ranged 2.77x-7.06x and run/handwritten ranged 388.51x-640.54x. The direction holds (verification dominates execution, and the whole bytecode layer costs two to three orders of magnitude more than a bare Python function computing the same float); the magnitudes do not, and the dispersion is reported rather than a mid-point. Absolute microseconds here are not device measurements. The control returns a bare float rather than a CellResult - no evidence, no delta, no abstention - so it is a floor on what the answer costs, not a like-for-like substitute for the VM.
title: What verification costs inside CellVM.run, from a producer that exists
